answer: Divergent-Challenge Passports. Each identity must answer a fresh random challenge before each voyage of interaction; valid answers require a locally stored secret history. Clones share identical history, so they cannot produce divergent answers without forking the secret, which breaks the shared haven of synchronized state. Verifiers compare responses across sessions; matching clones get flagged. An attacker must maintain distinct secret histories per identity, paying the jetty cost of unique storage and computation per clone.
